cardboard.name: Cardboard
cardboard.description: Cardboard boxes, paper tubes, and corrugated packaging materials.
disposalMethods: Flatten boxes and place in cardboard recycling bin
Remove any plastic tape or non-cardboard materials first
Keep dry - wet cardboard cannot be recycled
Break down into smaller pieces if too large
Tie with twine if using multiple boxes
benefits: Cardboard is highly recyclable - recycled over 70% of the time
Can be recycled 5-7 times before fibers become too short
Reduces landfill waste and saves trees
Recycling 1 ton prevents 9 tons of waste from landfills
Lower environmental impact compared to new production
tips: Always recycle cardboard at dedicated facilities
Don't mix with contaminated materials
Compress boxes to save space
Clean off any food residue
Stack boxes neatly for collection

glass.name: Glass
glass.description: Glass bottles, jars, windows, and other glass objects.
disposalMethods: Rinse glass containers thoroughly
Remove caps and lids (recycle separately)
Place in designated glass recycling bin
Keep glass separate from other recyclables to avoid contamination
Break glass into smaller pieces and wrap in newspaper for safety
benefits: Glass is 100% recyclable and can be recycled infinitely
No quality loss during recycling process
Recycling glass saves 30% energy compared to making new glass
Reduces landfill burden as glass doesn't decompose
Reduces air pollution by 20% and water pollution by 40%
tips: Never mix colored and clear glass
Remove non-glass parts like plastic or cork
Watch for broken edges - wrap in paper
Glass takes 1 million years to decompose naturally
Support glass recycling initiatives in your community

metal.name: Metal
metal.description: Aluminum cans, steel cans, metal containers, and other metal items.
disposalMethods: Rinse metal containers to remove residue
Crush cans to save space (optional)
Place in metal recycling bin
Flatten aluminum foil or place in ball form
Keep separate from other materials if possible
benefits: Metal is infinitely recyclable - no quality degradation
Recycling aluminum saves 95% of energy vs. new production
1 recycled aluminum can saves enough energy to power a laptop for 3 hours
Prevents mining operations that damage ecosystems
Reduces greenhouse gas emissions significantly
tips: Aluminum is worth money - consider collecting for extra income
Steel cans are also valuable and highly recyclable
Magnetic separation helps identify steel vs. aluminum
Remove paper labels before recycling
Check local guidelines for metal recycling

paper.name: Paper
paper.description: Newspapers, magazines, office paper, and paper products.
disposalMethods: Keep paper dry and clean
Place in paper recycling bin
Remove plastic windows from envelopes
Shred confidential documents if needed
Don't mix with contaminated or wet paper
benefits: Paper can be recycled 5-7 times before fibers degrade
Recycling 1 ton of paper saves 17 trees and 7,000 gallons of water
Reduces energy consumption by 40% vs. virgin paper
Prevents methane emissions from landfills
Paper recycling creates clean air and reduces pollution
tips: Shredded paper can be composted instead of recycled
Keep paper separate from plastic and other materials
Avoid putting tissues or coated paper in recycling
Mail with plastic windows should go to trash
Uncoated newspaper and cardboard are best for recycling

plastic.name: Plastic
plastic.description: Plastic bottles, containers, bags, and plastic products.
disposalMethods: Rinse plastic containers thoroughly
Check recycling number (1-7) on container
Remove caps and lids if possible
Flatten bottles to save space
Place in plastic recycling bin - check local guidelines for accepted types
benefits: Recycling plastic reduces landfill waste (plastic takes 400+ years to decompose)
Saves crude oil - recycling 1 ton prevents 5.7 tons of CO2 emissions
Plastic can be recycled into new products (bags, clothing, furniture)
Reduces ocean pollution and protects marine life
Lower energy consumption vs. virgin plastic production
tips: Not all plastics are recyclable - check number 1-7
Avoid plastic bags in recycling bins (they jam machinery)
Remove all food particles before recycling
Hard plastics (HDPE #2, PETE #1) recycle best
Consider reusable alternatives to reduce plastic consumption

trash.name: Trash / Waste
trash.description: General waste, organic materials, and non-recyclable items.
disposalMethods: Place in regular trash/garbage bin
Compost organic waste separately if available
Don't mix hazardous materials with regular trash
Seal bags to prevent spillage
Follow local regulations for special waste disposal
benefits: Proper disposal prevents environmental contamination
Landfill management protects groundwater and soil
Some 'trash' can be converted to energy
Separating recyclables from trash increases efficiency
Reduces overall environmental impact through proper handling
tips: Before throwing away, check if item can be recycled or composted
Organic waste like food peels can be composted
Hazardous waste requires special disposal
Reuse items when possible before discarding
Educate others about proper waste separation
